_comment: Reference copy of every setting at its shipped value. This file is NOT read at runtime —
the defaults live in config/Config.qml. Copy the keys you want into
~/.config/quickshell/ionix/config.json; that file is deep-merged over these and applied
live, so saving it restyles the running shell with no restart.
Arrays replace wholesale rather than appending.
Five layers are merged, lowest priority first: these defaults, then theme.json (written by
ionixtheme), then the active theme's option overlays (below), then settings.json (written
by the start menu's settings page — the only file the shell itself writes), then config.json
(yours). config.json therefore beats the settings page: a key you set by hand there makes the
matching switch inert, and the page shows those rows as 'Pinned by config.json' rather than
letting them flip and do nothing.
Theme options: a theme.json may declare an 'options' array, each entry
{ key, title, subtitle, glyph, default: bool, on: {config patch}, off: {config patch} },
which the settings page renders as a switch under 'Theme options'. Flipping one merges that
entry's 'on' or 'off' patch just above the theme's own values — so both files above still win
— and stores the value in settings.json under themes.<themename>.<key>, keyed by theme so
switching away and back keeps it. Both patches are optional: leaving 'off' out means the
theme's plain values already are the off state. Only booleans are rendered: a setting that is
genuinely one-of-N belongs in the settings page's own rows, where it applies under every theme
rather than only the one that thought to declare it — bar.position is the worked example.
Do not put 'options' here: options are declared by a theme, and these defaults are not one.

bar._comment: position is top | bottom | left | right, and is offered as a picker in the start menu's settings page for every theme — so a theme naming one here is stating a default, not a fact, and anything you pick there outlives a theme switch. The last two dock the bar to a screen edge as a vertical strip and every module stacks and re-anchors itself — popouts, menus and tooltips open sideways, the clock switches to clock.verticalFormat, and the taskbar and workspaces run top-to-bottom. `height` is the bar's THICKNESS whichever edge it is on, so it is the width of a vertical bar; Theme.pillHeight is derived from it and every module sizes its short axis to that. In `margin`, `top` is the gap at each end of the bar's long axis and `left` the gap from the edge it is docked to — a vertical bar swaps which is which, so the same two numbers keep meaning the same two gaps. All of it is ignored while floating is false.

modules._comment: Each name is a file in modules/. Beyond the ones listed, any theme may use the flat building blocks: StartButton (for Launcher), SearchBox, AppTaskbar (for Taskbar: pinned and running per app), TrayOverflow (for Tray), StatusCluster (for the indicators, opens QuickSettings), ClockCluster (for Clock and NotificationBell, opens NotificationCentre). They work on all four bar edges and under any palette.

theme._comment: Any key here overrides config/Theme.qml. Shown with the built-in values. Also accepted: flat (true: controls change colour rather than size, neutral hover fills, thin sliders), flyoutGap (px between a panel and the bar and screen edge; 0 is the shell's own placement), the derived surfaces as #AARRGGBB (barFill, panelFill, tooltipFill, pillFill, pillBorder, barBorder, panelBorder, divider, subtleHover, subtlePressed, controlFill, controlStroke, fieldFill, footerFill, closeHover, onAccent), and numbers for rSm, rPill, rPanel, pillHeight, fsXs to fsTitle, durFast to durSlow.

start._comment: The start menu behind the logo button. enabled:false gives the button back to launcher.command. layout "sections" is the home page with Pinned and Recommended at a fixed height over a footer strip; align "center" centres the menu on the screen, on a horizontal bar. maxHeightFraction is of the screen height — past that the menu body scrolls instead of growing. defaultPins is only a seed: as soon as you pin or unpin anything the list moves to $XDG_STATE_HOME/ionix/quickshell/start.json, which also holds the launch counts behind the Frequent section. Pins are desktop-entry ids without the '.desktop' suffix; ones naming apps you don't have are skipped, not drawn empty. The footer is titled with displayName, or when that is empty the account's full name (chfn -f), or the login; whenever the title is not the login, the login shows under it as user@host. avatar is a picture path (~ allowed); empty means the first of $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/quickshell/avatar.png and ~/.face that exists, re-checked every time the menu opens.

workspaces._comment: Workspaces are filtered to the monitor the bar is on. persistent pads the list with empty slots and is 0 by default because Hyprland assigns workspace IDs dynamically across monitors; raise it only with per-monitor workspace rules.

projects._comment: Project workspaces: save a workspace's apps and layout under a label and open them again later, with `ionix-project` (ships with Ionix; without it on PATH the feature hides itself). The label is the workspace's Hyprland name, so the bar shows it beside the dot (workspaces.showLabels) and the Alt+Tab cards carry it (windowSwitcher.showProjectLabels). showInStart adds the Projects section to the start menu's home page. Projects are JSON files in $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/ionix/projects, one per project, safe to edit by hand.

taskbar._comment: defaultPins seeds the AppTaskbar module's pinned apps, used until one is pinned or unpinned from it; the list then moves to start.json as taskbarPins. Same form as start.defaultPins.

media._comment: backend is mpris or off. preferred is a substring matched against an MPRIS player's identity or D-Bus name to pick one when several are running; empty means whichever is playing.

clock._comment: The vertical* formats are used instead when bar.position is left or right: 'HH:mm' at the bar font is wider than a 46px vertical bar, so the parts stack. Qt.formatDateTime passes anything it does not recognise through as a literal, which is how the embedded newline survives. timer is the countdown on the clock's right click: sound is played with pw-play and repeated beepGap ms after it ends until the pill is clicked; presets are lengths in seconds shown under the digits.

hue._comment: Philips Hue bar module, off by default. Set enabled:true and the bar shows a bulb; click it to find and pair a bridge. The bridge address and the credential it issues are NOT set here — they are written to $XDG_STATE_HOME/ionix/quickshell/hue.json along with your pinned lights, because this config is read-only. Lights are only polled while the popout is open, so pollInterval is a refresh rate you can see, not a background cost. cloudDiscovery:false skips discovery.meethue.com and leaves only manual IP entry.

calendar._comment: provider is none | local | outlook, and is offered as a picker in the settings page. local is the built-in read/write calendar (a JSON file, local.file, with simple daily/weekly/monthly/yearly repeats — add and edit events from the popout, or `ionix-calendar add`); a remote provider adds its account's events on top of the local ones rather than replacing them. Anything but none starts the ionix-calendar daemon as a child of the shell; it syncs every syncInterval seconds (and when the popout opens) into $XDG_STATE_HOME/ionix/quickshell/calendar/, which the popout reads — dots on days, a per-day agenda, a Join button on events with a link. showNext puts the next meeting in the clock pill when it starts within upcomingWindow minutes; reminders sends a notification reminderMinutes before each meeting. calendars is an include-list of calendar names or ids (`ionix-calendar calendars` prints them); empty means all. For outlook, clientId is your Entra app registration's Application (client) ID — a public client with device-code flow allowed, not a secret — and tenant is a tenant id/domain or organizations | consumers | common. Tokens go to the keyring via secret-tool, or a 0600 file under stateDir when there is no Secret Service.

backgrounds._comment: A picture behind the clock popout for the month on show: <dir>/<month>.png (or .jpg/.jpeg/.webp), named january..december or jan..dec, any case. It is cropped to cover the panel and darkened by dim (0 = untouched, 1 = the solid theme background) so the calendar stays readable. A month with no picture keeps the plain glass. dir "" means ~/.config/quickshell/ionix/calendar. Dropping a picture in place shows up the next time the popout opens.

dock._comment: The floating app dock (osd/DockWindow.qml), on any theme: pinned and running apps with the same pins as AppTaskbar. position is bottom, left, right or top. magnification is how much bigger the icon under the pointer gets, 1 for off. leading holds the shell's own items before the apps (appgrid, taskview); trailing holds more after a divider, each { title, icon, glyph, command }.

appGrid._comment: Every installed app as pages of big icons over the desktop (osd/AppGridOverlay.qml), with a search field: from the dock, start.opens or `qs -c ionix ipc call appgrid toggle`.

taskView._comment: Every window of the current workspace as thumbnails over a strip of all workspaces, from the TaskViewButton module, Super+Tab or `qs -c ionix ipc call taskview toggle`. It keeps clear of the bar and takes its look from the theme. maxCardWidth caps a lone window's thumbnail, in pixels.

windowSwitcher._comment: The Alt+Tab overlay. currentWorkspaceOnly:false offers every window everywhere in most-recently-used order, which is what the pre-overlay Alt+Tab bind reached; true narrows it to the focused workspace, Windows-style. livePreviews:false swaps the screencopy thumbnails for icon tiles — each visible card is otherwise a continuous capture stream. maxWidthFraction is of the screen width; past that the card grid wraps to further rows.

lock._comment: layout "bare" puts the picture, name and field on the wallpaper with the clock fixed near the top; "" is the password card. The lock screen, started by `ionix-lock` as its own Quickshell process (lock.qml) — it reads this same merged config, so it wears the active theme and follows it live while locked. background.image and background.video each take a path, or an object keyed by monitor name with "*" as the fallback. image may be a directory, which becomes a slideshow advancing every `interval` seconds; "" uses whatever awww is showing on that monitor. video is looped and muted, wins over image, needs qt6-multimedia-ffmpeg, and is skipped on battery unless videoOnBattery. blur and dim (0..1) apply while the password card is up. After screensaver.after idle seconds (0 = never) the card fades out, the picture clears and — with motion — slowly pans while the clock wanders. clockFormat "" follows clock.format. power adds suspend/restart/shut down buttons (the last two need a second click). fingerprint races fprintd against the password when a reader is present and stays silent when there isn't one.

power._comment: lock runs ionix-lock, which falls back to hyprlock by itself when the Quickshell lock screen cannot take the lock.
